To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the impacts of policies and project initiatives are highly context-dependent, that the same policy will have different effects in different contexts, and that the impacts of a given project are difficult to assess in the short-term.

(1) the Amazon region has undergone major ecological and social changes during the last 20 years, (2) the impacts of these changes are highly variable and depend on the local context, (3) no policy has been able to untie this ‘Gordian Knot’, and (4) the sense of place and cultural factors play a more important part in shaping the perception of the local population than economic factors.

(i) the subregional contexts in which development projects are implemented are very important in shaping their impacts; (ii) the impacts of these projects are mixed, and they often lead to trade-offs between social development and environmental conservation; and (iii) the cultural factors and a strong sense of place are more important than economic factors in the evaluation of the quality of life of local communities in the Amazon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How can we assess and monitor the impact of policies and initiatives aimed at sustainable development?
the development of a cross-disciplinary indicator system that can be used to assess the impact of development initiatives on the environment and on local populations.
the following questions: How can we measure the impacts of development projects in a way that allows for comparison across sites and contexts?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sustainable development in the region is still far from being a reality, and that the Amazon is still in the process of being transformed by the development of a new frontier economy.
sustainable development in the Brazilian Amazon is a myth.
, in the Amazon, the sustainable development of the local population remains a challenge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DURAMAX indicator system is a cross-disciplinary, comparative tool for assessing the impact of regional policies and projects at local and sub-regional levels.
we are still a long way from achieving sustainable development in the Brazilian Amazon, but we are getting there.

the Amazonian region is a laboratory of sustainable development, where the results are mixed and where it seems that the best way to achieve sustainable development is to promote a diversity of projects, each of them adapted to its local context and to the needs and aspirations of local people.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DURAMAX system can provide an effective and replicable approach for assessing and comparing sustainable development at the local and subreginal levels, and for understanding the complex interactions between social and environmental factors.
the DURAMZ indicator system is a valuable tool to help policy-makers and project managers better understand the impacts of their initiatives and to improve the design of future policies.
a holistic view of the impacts of development policies and projects is necessary to better understand and improve the sustainability of the Amazon.
